findings.summary: Page 2 opens with a `git worktree` recipe three pages before worktrees are introduced or defined.
findings.evidence: Page 2, first block: `git worktree add -b hotfix-501 \` / `  ../hotfix origin/main` / `# fix, test, push` / `git worktree remove ../hotfix` — while "Your First Worktree" (`git worktree add ../hotfix hotfix-br`, "Second directory, same `.git` object database") does not appear until page 5.
findings.fix: Delete this block from page 2 and place the hotfix recipe on page 6 alongside "Review A PR, Tree Untouched", after worktrees have been defined; open page 2 with the "Look Before You Restore" heading.

findings.summary: Page 1 ends with the dropped-stash recovery recipe, before `drop`, unreachable objects, or gc are taught, and it is repeated verbatim on page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 1, final block: `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` / `git show <sha>        # identify it` / `git stash apply <sha>` — with no heading; page 4 repeats it under "Recover A Dropped Stash" as `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` / `git stash apply <sha>`.
findings.fix: Remove the block from page 1 (it has no heading and depends on pages 2–4), keeping the single copy under "Recover A Dropped Stash" on page 4.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: A headingless bullet group about moving work to a new branch sits under the gc-lifetime table and refers to commands that appear nowhere on page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 3, after the reflog/gc table: "Stash, make the branch, pop — three commands" / "Works because stash is ==per-repository==" / "The base commit still has to be close" — but page 3 contains no stash/branch/pop commands; the three-command sequence is on page 2 under "Wrong Branch? Move It".
findings.fix: Move these four bullets to page 2 directly beneath the `git stash push -u` / `git switch -c correct-branch` / `git stash pop` block they describe, and replace them on page 3 with the recovery-window consequence the gc table implies.

findings.summary: Stash-flag teaching starts headingless at the bottom of page 4 and is then taught again from scratch on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 4 tail bullets: "`-u` stores untracked as the third parent", "`-a` near `node_modules/` stashes gigabytes", "`-k` leaves the staged version on disk" — then page 5 re-teaches the same flags under "What Gets Swept Up" (table rows `(none)`/`-u`/`-a`) and "Keep-Index Pre-Commit Test".
findings.fix: Cut the `-u`/`-a`/`-k` bullets and the "Surgical Stashing" block from page 4 and merge them into page 5 under "What Gets Swept Up" and the `-p`/pathspec bullets already there; end page 4 at the "Default Move" block.

findings.summary: The title "Recovery, apply vs pop" omits the stash-flag material that fills the last quarter of the page, which is instead promised by page 5's title.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with blocks covering "`-u` stores untracked as the third parent", "`-a` near `node_modules/` stashes gigabytes", "`-k` leaves the staged version on disk" and the heading "Surgical Stashing" (`git stash push -p`, pathspec form) — none of which is "Recovery, apply vs pop", while page 5 is titled "Stash Flags & Your First Worktree".
findings.fix: Retitle page 4 to "Recovery, apply vs pop & Stash Flags" (or move the `-u`/`-a`/`-k`/`-p` blocks onto page 5 and leave the title as-is).
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: Page 1 asserts that stash indices renumber on drop before `drop` has been introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 1, "Your First Stash" bullets: "Indices renumber whenever an entry is dropped" — `git stash drop stash@{2}` is first shown on page 2 under "Restore, Keep Or Kill".
findings.fix: Cut the bullet from page 1 and keep the renumbering point on page 2, where it already appears as "Drop `stash@{0}` and old `{1}` becomes `{0}`".

findings.summary: Page 1's title "The Context-Switch Problem" does not cover the stash tutorial and dropped-stash recovery that close the page.
findings.evidence: Page 1's final blocks are the heading "Your First Stash" with `git stash push -m "wip: parser fix"` and a recovery snippet `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` / `git stash apply <sha>` — the latter repeated verbatim on page 4.
findings.fix: Drop the duplicated `git fsck --unreachable` recovery snippet from page 1 (it is already page 4's content) and extend the title to "The Context-Switch Problem & Your First Stash".

findings.summary: `git stash branch` is explained in terms of the stash's parent commit two blocks before stash parents are defined.
findings.evidence: Page 2, "The Clean Rescue": "# branch at the stash's parent commit" — the parent structure ("parent 1 = HEAD at stash time", "parent 2 = index / staged state") is introduced later on the same page under "A Stash Entry Is A Commit".
findings.fix: Move "The Clean Rescue" block to after the "A Stash Entry Is A Commit" diagram and its parent bullets.

findings.summary: Page 2 opens with a worktree add/remove snippet that its title "Restore Commands & Stash Anatomy" does not describe.
findings.evidence: The first block on page 2 is `git worktree add -b hotfix-501 \ ../hotfix origin/main` … `git worktree remove ../hotfix`, before the heading "Look Before You Restore".
findings.fix: Move that worktree snippet to page 5 ("Your First Worktree") so page 2 starts at "Look Before You Restore" and matches its title.

findings.summary: `--staged` is called an exact mirror of `--keep-index`, but `--keep-index` still records the staged changes in the stash entry, so the two differ in what is saved.
findings.evidence: "Exactly the mirror of `--keep-index`" — git-stash(1) for `--keep-index` only promises "All changes already added to the index are left intact" in the tree; the entry itself is a full stash of staged + unstaged work, whereas `--staged` "Stash only the changes that are currently staged."
findings.fix: Change to "Mirror of `--keep-index` in what stays on disk — but note `-k` still stores the staged changes in the entry, so a later `pop` reapplies them; `--staged` does not save the unstaged work at all."

findings.summary: The yellow sticky note's pin graphic overlaps the code block and obscures a character of the trailing comment.
findings.evidence: Code line reads "new=$(git rev-parse -q --verify \ refs/stash)   # same = no-op" — the pink pin of the "exits 0 even when nothing saved" sticky sits on top of the "n" in "no-op".
findings.fix: Shift the sticky note (and its pin anchor) down or left so it clears the last code line of the `old=$(git rev-parse ...)` block, or drop the trailing `# same = no-op` comment so nothing sits under the pin.

findings.summary: Page 5 bullets reference `prune` and `worktree move`, neither of which is introduced until page 6.
findings.evidence: Page 5, final bullets: "`move` fixes internal path pointers — never `mv`" and "`lock` stops prune reaping unmounted storage" — `git worktree prune   # after a manual rm` and `git worktree move ../old ../new` first appear in page 6's "Administration" block.
findings.fix: Keep only the `lock` bullet on page 5 ("stops a worktree on unmounted storage being reaped" without naming prune) and move the `move` bullet to page 6 directly under the "Administration" code block.

findings.summary: The bisect recipe relies on the per-worktree ref scope before that scope is defined on page 7.
findings.evidence: Page 6: "`refs/bisect/*` is ==per-worktree==, so it stays there" — the per-worktree vs shared ref table (rows `HEAD`, `refs/bisect/*`, `refs/worktree/*`, `branches, tags`, `refs/stash`) is on page 7.
findings.fix: Move the per-worktree/shared ref table to page 6 ahead of "Bisect Somewhere Else", or reword the bullet to state the fact plainly ("bisect state lives in this worktree only") and let page 7 name the ref namespace.

findings.summary: The dangerous `--force` override for the one-branch-one-checkout rule is taught a full page before the safe fix.
findings.evidence: Page 6: "Hard rule: ==one branch, one checkout== at a time" / "`--force` overrides that hard rule" — while "Fix: `--detach`, or a new branch off it" and `git worktree add --detach ../scratch main` do not appear until page 7's "The #1 Worktree Error".
findings.fix: Add the `--detach`/new-branch fix to page 6 immediately after the hard-rule bullet, so the safe remedy precedes the `--force` escape hatch.

findings.summary: The claim that branch switching destroys build directories is wrong — gitignored/untracked artifacts survive a checkout, which the deck itself states on page 1.
findings.evidence: "10-minute build: switching kills `node_modules`", "Also `target/`, `__pycache__`, compiler caches" — but page 1's sidebox says of untracked and ignored files: "Branch switch ignores them ... They survive the switch and collide".
findings.fix: Restate the mechanism: "switching rewrites tracked sources, so the 10-minute build is invalidated (and a changed lockfile forces a reinstall) — `node_modules/`, `target/`, `__pycache__` are not deleted, they go stale."

findings.summary: The doubled-disk figure for a second clone ignores that a clone from a local path hardlinks objects by default, so it does not copy the 2 GB object store.
findings.evidence: "A 2 GB `.git` clone becomes 4 GB on disk" — git-clone(1): for a local source, "The files under .git/objects/ directory are hardlinked to save space when possible" (default `--local`).
findings.fix: Qualify it: "Re-cloning from the remote turns a 2 GB `.git` into 4 GB on disk; a local `git clone /path` hardlinks objects instead, but only on the same filesystem and with `--no-hardlinks` off."

findings.summary: Storage cost understates a stash entry as one commit; a normal entry is two commits and three with `-u`/`-a`.
findings.evidence: "One commit + trees + blobs per stash entry" — contradicted by the deck's own page 2 ("parent 1 = HEAD at stash time / parent 2 = index / staged state / parent 3 = untracked, only with -u") and page 10 ("Stash = hidden 2-or-3-parent commits"); `git stash create` writes an index commit, an optional untracked commit, and the stash commit.
findings.fix: Change to "Two commits per entry (three with `-u`) + trees + blobs".
